argv: Added the independently compiling capability-driven memory fabric with bounded registration/concurrency, exact revision/capability routing, typed request preflight, active/observer separation, and no provider-specific or TraceDecay-internal coupling.

Evidence: crates/tracedecay-memory-fabric depends only on tracedecay-memory-provider-api and implements finite FabricConfig, typed FabricError, stable registration state, deterministic provider status, lock-free bounded call permits, exact revision and capability checks, cancellation/deadline preflight, compatible handshake validation, active invocation, and observation-only delivery. ObserverReceipt intentionally strips provider payloads/extensions so observer values are unreachable from context by type. No worker, queue, transport, persistence, DB/code-index/daemon/host dependency, global singleton, provider-name conditional, or fallback exists. Strict Rust tests cover bounded/duplicate/mismatched registration, capability-driven active calls, missing optional capability, structural observer isolation, disabled/revision failures before provider contact, cancellation/deadline non-contact, deterministic ordering, and finite concurrent permits. Workspace/lock wiring is generated and convergence-mapped; product ownership policy and checker recognize the additive fabric crate. Metadata, fmt, Clippy -D warnings, tests, provider API regression, M1 binding drift, patch budget, dependency graph, and concrete-provider scanner all pass.
